claims.text: Coating tungsten particles with an ultra-thin, continuous graphene layer before consolidation will increase the effective thermal conductivity of a W–Cu composite.
The graphene-coated W–Cu composite will retain mechanical durability relative to an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite.
The graphene-coated W–Cu composite will retain irradiation resistance relative to an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite.
Applying a continuous graphene coating to tungsten particles will create a graphene-containing interface at the tungsten–copper boundary after consolidation.
Graphene possesses exceptionally high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Graphene possesses robust intrinsic mechanical properties.
Metal–graphene interfaces can increase strength in Cu/graphene and Al/graphene composites by affecting dislocation cross-slip or nucleation.
A conformal graphene coating reduces thermal boundary resistance at the W–Cu interface.
The graphene coating enhances phonon transport across the W–Cu interface.
The graphene coating enhances electron transport across the W–Cu interface.
The graphene layer can arrest crack propagation in the W–Cu composite.
The graphene layer can mitigate radiation-induced degradation of the W–Cu interface.
The graphene-coated composite will show an appreciable increase in effective thermal conductivity compared with an uncoated W–Cu control.
The graphene-coated composite will maintain similar mechanical strength under fusion-reactor conditions compared with the uncoated control.
The graphene-coated composite will maintain similar irradiation resistance under fusion-reactor conditions compared with the uncoated control.
The proposed enhancement should hold in fusion-reactor and high-heat-flux operating environments.
Extremely high irradiation doses or prolonged elevated-temperature exposure might degrade the graphene layer and limit its effectiveness.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thermal-conductivity improvement, or observation of reduced post-treatment mechanical strength or irradiation resistance, would falsify the hypothesis.
